This page lists the spec and status fields of Bucket, each with its type, its limits and its description. The [Platform page](../../../platform/services/bucket.md) explains the concept, and the `metadata` of every kind is [the same](../../common-definitions.md#objectmeta).

## Bucket

::include[../../../../../api/types/v1alpha1/examples/bucket/bucket.yaml#bucket]

| apiVersion | kind |
| --- | --- |
| `funcd.io/v1alpha1` | `Bucket` |

### `Bucket.spec`

| Field | Type and limits | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `prefixes` | array of [`Bucket.spec.prefixes[]`](#bucketspecprefixes), required | The Bucket's prefixes, each a key space with its own owner and cap. Prefix names are unique within the Bucket. A Function or a Lake that binds a prefix the Bucket does not list waits, with the reason BucketNotFound. |
| `quota` | object, [`Bucket.spec.quota`](#bucketspecquota) | Caps on the Bucket's total size and on each object. While the Bucket has a size cap, funcd refuses to sign a presigned PUT URL for it, with 403. |

### `Bucket.spec.prefixes[]`

| Field | Type and limits | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string, required, a DNS-1123 label | The prefix's name, unique within the Bucket. Over S3, it is the first segment of each object's key. |
| `owner` | object, [`Bucket.spec.prefixes[].owner`](#bucketspecprefixesowner) | The one Function or Lake that may write the prefix, besides the writers that a RolesAssignment names. In a Bucket that a Function or a Lake declares by name, an omitted owner is that Function or Lake. The prefix that a Site serves its bundle from must have no owner, since the Site writes its builds there; the prefixes of a Site's ingress rules may have one. |
| `quota` | object, [`Bucket.spec.prefixes[].quota`](#bucketspecprefixesquota) | A cap on the prefix's total size: a write into the prefix must fit both this cap and the Bucket's, and while it is set funcd refuses to sign a presigned PUT URL into the prefix, with 403. It also caps a Lake's files under the prefix, though not the Lake's catalog. |

### `Bucket.spec.prefixes[].owner`

| Field | Type and limits | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | string, required, one of `Function`, `Lake` | The writer's kind. A Function and a Lake may share a name, so the kind says which one writes. |
| `name` | string, required, a DNS-1123 label | The writer's name, in the Bucket's namespace. In a Workflow's buckets, a Function owner names a step and a Lake owner a lake that the Workflow declares. |

### `Bucket.spec.prefixes[].quota`

| Field | Type and limits | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `maxBytes` | integer, at least 0 | The same cap as a number of bytes. Set maxSize or maxBytes, not both. |
| `maxSize` | string, a size: 1 to 15 digits and an optional binary unit, Ki, Mi, Gi or Ti, with or without a B (512Ki, 2GiB) | The cap on the total size held, above zero. Set maxSize or maxBytes, not both; neither means no cap. A write that would pass the cap gets 507 in a KV store or a Bucket; a SQL execute call gets 507 once the database holds the cap. |

### `Bucket.spec.quota`

| Field | Type and limits | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `maxBytes` | integer, at least 0 | The same cap as a number of bytes. Set maxSize or maxBytes, not both. |
| `maxObjectBytes` | integer, at least 0 | The largest object a write may store, in bytes. A larger write gets 413, or EntityTooLarge over S3, and while it is set funcd refuses to sign a presigned PUT URL for the Bucket, with 403. 0 sets no cap of the Bucket's own, so only funcd's upload limits apply, such as s3gateway.maxUploadBytes. |
| `maxSize` | string, a size: 1 to 15 digits and an optional binary unit, Ki, Mi, Gi or Ti, with or without a B (512Ki, 2GiB) | The cap on the total size held, above zero. Set maxSize or maxBytes, not both; neither means no cap. A write that would pass the cap gets 507 in a KV store or a Bucket; a SQL execute call gets 507 once the database holds the cap. |

## Handler API

The methods a handler calls on its context's clients, in each language funcd ships a shim for.

### `ctx.blob`

#### TypeScript

The Bucket prefixes that the function binds, by alias: read, write, delete and list their objects, whose keys are relative to the binding's prefix.

| Method | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `get(binding: string, key: string): Promise<Uint8Array \| null>` | The object's content as bytes, or null when the object does not exist. |
| `put(binding: string, key: string, value: Uint8Array): Promise<void>` | Writes the object, replacing any object with that key. The value is at most 64 MiB, and at most the Bucket's spec.quota.maxObjectBytes when that is set: a larger one fails with the HTTP status 413. Only the prefix's owner and the writers that a RolesAssignment names can write. |
| `del(binding: string, key: string): Promise<void>` | Deletes the object, and fails with the HTTP status 404 when it does not exist. Only the prefix's owner and the writers that a RolesAssignment names can delete. |
| `list(binding: string, prefix?: string): Promise<string[]>` | The keys that start with prefix; without a prefix, every key under the binding's prefix. |
| `signedUrl(binding: string, key: string, opts?: SignOptions): Promise<string>` | A presigned URL that lets its holder send an opts.method request, GET by default, for the object until opts.expiry passes: a duration such as "10m" or "1h30m", in whole seconds from 1s to 168h, or 15 minutes when unset. Any other expiry, "" included, fails with the HTTP status 400. A PUT or DELETE URL needs permission to write the prefix, and a PUT URL fails with the HTTP status 403 when the Bucket sets maxObjectBytes or a size quota applies to the Bucket or the prefix, since funcd could not enforce it on the upload. No blob store that funcd opens signs URLs, so a call that passes these checks fails with the HTTP status 503. |

Each method here that calls funcd can also fail with the status 500 and the problem type `urn:funcd:problem:internal`, when funcd meets an error that it did not expect; funcd logs its cause.

#### Python

The Bucket prefixes that the function binds, by alias: read, write, delete and list their objects, whose keys are relative to the binding's prefix.

| Method | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `get(binding: str, key: str) -> bytes \| None` | The object's content as bytes, or ``None`` when the object does not exist. |
| `put(binding: str, key: str, data: bytes) -> None` | Writes the object, replacing any object with that key. ``data`` is at most 64 MiB, and at most the Bucket's ``spec.quota.maxObjectBytes`` when that is set: a larger one fails with the HTTP status 413. Only the prefix's owner and the writers that a RolesAssignment names can write. |
| `delete(binding: str, key: str) -> None` | Deletes the object, and fails with the HTTP status 404 when it does not exist. Only the prefix's owner and the writers that a RolesAssignment names can delete. |
| `list(binding: str, prefix: str = '') -> list[str]` | The keys that start with ``prefix``; without a prefix, every key under the binding's prefix. |
| `signed_url(binding: str, key: str, method: str = 'GET', expiry: str \| None = None) -> str` | A presigned URL that lets its holder send a ``method`` request for the object until ``expiry`` passes: a duration string such as ``"10m"`` or ``"1h30m"``, in whole seconds from 1s to 168h, or 15 minutes when ``None``. A method other than ``GET``, ``PUT`` or ``DELETE``, or any other expiry, ``""`` included, fails with the HTTP status 400; an ``expiry`` that is not a string raises ``TypeError`` before any request. A ``PUT`` or ``DELETE`` URL needs permission to write the prefix, and a ``PUT`` URL fails with the HTTP status 403 when the Bucket sets ``maxObjectBytes`` or a size quota applies to the Bucket or the prefix, since funcd could not enforce it on the upload. No blob store that funcd opens signs URLs, so a call that passes these checks fails with the HTTP status 503. |

Each method here that calls funcd can also fail with the status 500 and the problem type `urn:funcd:problem:internal`, when funcd meets an error that it did not expect; funcd logs its cause.
